title: JWT verify calls each emit one structured audit event on the fixed allow-list
asA: operator running the runtime-verify suite against the JWT verifier
iWant: every verify call to write one structured `keycloak.jwt` event carrying only the allow-list fields
soThat: the audit stream stays free of token material and every refusal has a stable reasonClass a reviewer can gate on

acceptanceCriteria.description: A verified JWT emits exactly one `keycloak.jwt` audit event carrying `outcome=verified` and the caller's realm slug; no token value appears.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a JWT signed by realm `alpha`'s current signing key whose `iss`, `aud`, and `exp` claims match the configured verification record
acceptanceCriteria.when: the JWT verifier verifies the token
acceptanceCriteria.then: the audit sink records exactly one event whose own-property keys are exactly `{family, outcome, realmSlug, at}` with `family=keycloak.jwt` and `outcome=verified`; no access token, id token, refresh token, introspection response body, client secret, raw claim record, or substring of any of the above appears in any field

acceptanceCriteria.description: A refused JWT emits exactly one `keycloak.jwt` audit event carrying `outcome=refused` and a `reasonClass` from the fixed set.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a JWT whose `exp` has passed against realm `alpha`
acceptanceCriteria.when: the JWT verifier verifies the token
acceptanceCriteria.then: the audit sink records exactly one event whose `outcome` is `refused` and `reasonClass` is exactly one of `expired`, `issuer_mismatch`, `audience_mismatch`, `signature_invalid`; the event carries `family=keycloak.jwt`, `realmSlug=alpha`, and `at`; no token or claim material appears in any field

acceptanceCriteria.description: A JWKS-refresh retry on `signature_invalid` before re-verifying emits exactly one refused event and, on a successful second verify, one verified event; no third event is written for the retry itself.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a JWT whose signature does not verify against the cached JWKS but does verify against the freshly-refreshed JWKS (a key-rollover window)
acceptanceCriteria.when: the JWT verifier refuses on cache, refreshes the JWKS per its documented posture, and re-verifies
acceptanceCriteria.then: the audit sink records exactly two events in order: one `keycloak.jwt` event with `outcome=refused` and `reasonClass=signature_invalid`, then one `keycloak.jwt` event with `outcome=verified`; the retry itself is not recorded as a distinct event

acceptanceCriteria.description: A sink failure during the emission of a `keycloak.jwt` event does not mask the underlying verify outcome; the mechanism records a `keycloak.audit_sink_failed` warning event and the verify outcome is unchanged.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a valid JWT against realm `alpha` and an audit sink whose write throws
acceptanceCriteria.when: the JWT verifier emits the completion event
acceptanceCriteria.then: the verifier's return value still reports the underlying refusal or verification result unchanged; the mechanism records a `keycloak.audit_sink_failed` warning event carrying the realm slug and a reason-class string; no token value or raw claim record appears in any field
